core_obligations: Set up the affine descriptions (proof lines 5364-5423): write X = Spec(A), Y = Spec(B) and, for an affine V = Spec(C) etale over Y, compute the pullback g^{-1}h_V and the sheaf h_{X x_Y V} in terms of the ring maps, obtaining a map between them from the morphism of topoi.

Show the comparison map is an isomorphism (proof lines 5426-5450): the small etale site of X has enough points, so the map of sheaves g^{-1}h_V -> h_{X x_Y V} can be checked on stalks, where it becomes the corresponding statement about the residue field points of X and the etale algebras over B.

Show the isomorphisms are functorial (proof lines 5453-5495): for a morphism V_1 -> V_2 of affine etale Y-schemes, the resulting squares commute, so the assignment V maps to X x_Y V defines a functor on the full subcategory of affine etale Y-schemes, which by the affine description gives a morphism of schemes f : X -> Y.

Identify the pushforwards (proof lines 5498-5522): for every sheaf F on X_etale, the isomorphisms obtained above give a natural identification f_{small, *}F = g_*F, because both are computed by evaluating on affine etale Y-schemes and the descriptions agree there.

Compare the structural maps (proof lines 5525-5547): through this identification one checks that f_{small}^sharp and g^sharp agree, which is exactly the assertion that (g, g^sharp) is 2-isomorphic to (f_{small}, f_{small}^sharp); uniqueness follows because a morphism of schemes is determined by its underlying morphism of small ringed topoi.
proof_roadmap: Write both schemes as spectra of rings and compute the two sheaves involved over an affine etale Y-scheme.
Use that the small etale site of X has enough points to identify the comparison map with an isomorphism on stalks.
Check functoriality in the affine etale variable, which assembles a morphism of schemes f : X -> Y with X x_Y V = g^{-1}h_V.
Identify the pushforwards of f_{small} and g, and then the structural maps, obtaining the 2-isomorphism.
Conclude uniqueness from the faithfulness of the small ringed topos of a scheme.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reconstructs a morphism of schemes from its induced morphism of locally ringed small etale topoi, for affine X and Y (statement lines 5346-5362). The proof has five genuinely separate steps. It first computes the pullback g^{-1}h_V and the representable sheaf h_{X x_Y V} in ring terms for affine V = Spec(C) etale over Y (proof lines 5375-5423); it then shows the comparison map is an isomorphism by testing on stalks, using that the small etale site of X has enough points (proof lines 5426-5450); it checks functoriality in V so that the assignment V maps to X x_Y V is a functor of affine etale Y-schemes and yields a morphism of schemes f : X -> Y (proof lines 5453-5495); it identifies f_{small, *} with g_* through the same affine descriptions (proof lines 5498-5522); and finally it compares the structural maps to obtain the 2-isomorphism, with uniqueness following from the faithfulness of the construction (proof lines 5525-5547). The claim is H2: a long but entirely elementary argument, in which each step is written out and no step is delegated.
